articles.title: IPL media rights: Industry seeks best price-discovery models
articles.summary: Cricket News: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to .
articles.body: Last week, the ICC sounded the media-rights bugle by appointing a five-member working group. The group’s top priority in the coming months will be to consider all possible steps that can help the ICC retain the existing value for the 2028-31 cycle, or even better it, by exploring the best price-discovery models available. The ICC’s media-rights tender, however, will not be the first to hit the market. The world governing body will have to wait for the BCCI to first draft and release the IPL media-rights tender, following which any other property around the world, including the ICC, will come up for sale.Meanwhile, the BCCI is yet to act on it. The Indian cricket administration, usually considered a sleeping giant unless woken from its slumber, hasn’t taken a call yet on bringing a financial agency on board to figure out the right price-discovery models, as it did during the previous rights cycle. Interestingly, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia is on the ICC media rights working group, which ECB chief Richard Thompson is heading and also includes ICC chairman Jay Shah.In 2022, the cricket board brought in financial advisory firm KPMG to draft the IPL tender document. This document included a special non-exclusive digital-rights package designed for selling a select ‘bouquet’ of high-value matches in the Indian subcontinent. Set at 18 matches per season for a 74-game structure, this package alone rose to Rs 3,273 crore at Rs 33.24 crore per game and ensured Internet rights ended up generating more revenue for the BCCI from the subcontinent for the first time in history than the traditional sale of TV rights.“We were expecting to hear something from them (BCCI) on this. Given the way tech is changing how we consume sport, we thought the board would be keen to explore these changing revenue patterns and models for IPL. Look at the YouTube sports-bundling model in the US, for instance. The NFL Sunday Ticket is a case study in itself,” said an industry executive.Sports industry executives strongly believe that the value can be tremendous if the BCCI explores this space in greater detail. The BCCI members will be in Mumbai starting on Friday for the AGM. Those tracking developments can’t think of a more important subject the members may need to discuss than the upcoming sale of media rights.“India has a strong cricket platform. The IPL is already a premium property on that platform. All you need to build on it is effectively what can be done outside of the live match feed. Archives, highlights, documentaries, regional storytelling, fan engagement etc. You may have one or two broadcasters in the race for rights but building a separate non-live consumer base to monetise premium properties selectively is another subject matter altogether,” the executive added.The key aligning principle here must be based on a modular concept, rather than the all-inclusive one that currently prevails. “Perhaps not a very healthy model either, considering all your eggs happen to be in one single basket,” says an IPL franchise executive, referring to IPL’s heavy leaning on JioStar for live broadcasts. OTT giant Netflix hasn’t majorly dabbled with the idea of putting live sport behind its paywall. However, it has certainly not backed away from exploring events that can be included within its existing plans to create a reason for people to remain subscribed.“We keep wondering why an Amazon or a Netflix or a YouTube hasn’t looked at the India market. Well, the fact is, the onus lies on us to market our products to them and only then can we catch their attention. So, in the case of IPL rights, the onus certainly lies on the BCCI to go out and start talking to these platforms,” the franchise executive added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Clear message’ for Hardik Pandya: Gautam Gambhir reveals what the all-rounder must do to return to Team India
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through gam.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has made it clear that Hardik Pandya will have to build his way back into international cricket through game time, with the all-rounder currently not part of India's squads after not playing enough cricket since the IPL.Following India's 127-run win over Afghanistan in the third T20I in New Delhi on Thursday, Gambhir said Pandya's immediate priority should be getting back on the field, including through the India A series, before pushing for a return to the senior sides."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs, and he hasn't played a lot of cricket since the IPL, so we don't want to push him into international cricket because international cricket can be extremely tough on your body as well," Gambhir said during the post-match press conference.The India head coach also revealed that the message to Pandya has been straightforward: play, regain match fitness and then push for a place in both white-ball squads."And that was the clear message to him that if he can play that India A series, and then if everything goes well, he can come back and be part of the T20s and the one-day squad as well," Gambhir said.India could play Hardik and Nitish togetherGambhir's comments also highlighted India's plans to develop more than one seam-bowling all-rounder. Nitish Kumar Reddy, initially included in India's 15-member Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn from the continental event and will instead feature in the ODI series against the West Indies.Gambhir believes the move will give Reddy valuable game time and accelerate his development with the ball ahead of India's future assignments."From Nitish's point of view, it's actually a great thing that he's been withdrawn from the T20 format, and he'll get game time against the West Indies as well," he said. "We know how important a seam-bowling all-rounder will probably be in a year and when we go to South Africa. And once Hardik comes back, obviously it's going to be good."The coach even suggested India could eventually accommodate both Pandya and Reddy in the same playing XI."Sometimes we could even go on to play both of them in the playing 11," Gambhir said, while stressing that Pandya's current bowling workload remains a factor."Hardik at the moment cannot bowl 10 overs," he added.Reddy's bowling development excites GambhirGambhir was encouraged by Reddy's progress as a seam-bowling all-rounder and believes having multiple players who can contribute with both bat and ball will give India greater flexibility."I think it's good that we got Nitish now from the Asian Games so that now he can, and you could see the more he bowls, the better he becomes, and we have when you can develop a couple of seam-bowling all-rounders, it will always be handy," Gambhir said.Reddy will now get an opportunity to feature in the ODI series against the West Indies rather than the Asian Games, providing him with additional match exposure.Abhishek's hundred powers India to 3-0 sweepThe Hardik discussion came after India completed a commanding 3-0 T20I series sweep over Afghanistan. Abhishek Sharma smashed a record-breaking 108 off just 34 balls as India posted 221/7 in the third match in New Delhi.Ravi Bishnoi and Reddy then claimed three wickets each as Afghanistan were bowled out for 94, their lowest total against India in T20Is and their heaviest defeat in the format.Gambhir, however, said the focus inside the dressing room remained on impact rather than individual milestones."I can sit here and keep talking about his 100, but it's just the impact. The only thing we talk about in that dressing room is how much impact we create with the bat and how much impact we can create with the ball," Gambhir said.India's 100 runs in the powerplay was another major positive for Gambhir."T20 cricket is not about runs or wickets; it's about how much impact you can create," he said. "The biggest positive was we got a 100 in the powerplay that we have never done in my coaching tenure."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mohammad Rizwan approaches ICC Anti-Corruption Unit over mobile phone seizure by Pakistan's cyber crime agency
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corrupti.
articles.body: Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) for clarity over the seizure of his mobile phone by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). The move comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed his petition challenging the agency’s notices, leaving the Pakistan cricketer seeking answers over the handling of his device and the procedures followed during the ongoing inquiry.According to sources quoted by Geo News, Rizwan submitted an online request through the ICC ACU portal, asking whether the ICC or the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) was aware of, or involved in, the action taken against him.Rizwan seeks clarity over ICC anti-corruption proceduresSources said Rizwan’s request was not intended as a complaint against any individual or organisation. Instead, the Pakistan batter has sought clarification on the procedures followed in his case and the role, if any, of the ICC or ECB in the seizure of his mobile phone.The former Pakistan white-ball captain has also asked whether the process of requesting his phone, transferring it from England to Pakistan and conducting a forensic examination was in accordance with the ICC Anti-Corruption Code.Rizwan has further sought guidance on his responsibilities and the steps he should follow while cooperating with anti-corruption authorities in the future.Lahore High Court dismisses Rizwan’s petitionThe development comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwan’s petition challenging notices issued to him by the NCCIA. During Thursday’s hearing, Rizwan’s lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, told Chief Justice Aalia Neelum that the cricketer had been called to a hotel lobby after the Lord’s Test in England and questioned without being served a notice.According to his counsel, Rizwan’s mobile phone was taken into custody after he was assured that it would be returned within three hours. However, the device has not yet been returned.Rizwan’s lawyer also questioned the NCCIA’s jurisdiction, arguing that the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit was the appropriate forum for matters involving alleged corruption-related violations by cricketers. The court directed Rizwan to respond to the NCCIA’s notice before dismissing his petition.NCCIA probe linked to betting and alleged dressing-room leaksThe NCCIA notice relates to an inquiry into online betting and gambling in Pakistan cricket. Reports have also linked the investigation to alleged leaks of information from the Pakistan dressing room during the Test series against England.Rizwan and fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq appeared before the agency in Lahore earlier this month as part of the investigation.No final findings against Rizwan or Imam have been officially announced.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shree Charani’s four-for, Shafali's quick 40 help India beat Japan in Asian Games quater-finals
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their pl.
articles.body: India Women produced a dominant all-round performance to thrash Japan by eight wickets in the quarter-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, booking their place in the semi-finals against Bangladesh.The result also sets up a repeat of the Women’s Asia Cup 2026 semi-final line-up, with Sri Lanka set to face Pakistan in the other last-four clash.Shree Charani stars as Japan are bowled out for 57After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers dismantled Japan’s batting line-up, restricting the hosts to just 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the charge with a remarkable spell of 4/10, including two maiden overs, to register the best bowling figures by an Indian at the Asian Games. Shafali Verma also chipped in with two wickets for 13 runs.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 balls, but the hosts struggled to build partnerships against India’s disciplined attack.Shafali and Richa wrap up chase in five oversIndia’s chase was emphatic, as they reached the target in just five overs, finishing at 59/2 and winning with 90 balls to spare. Shafali Verma set the tone with a blistering 40 off 15 balls, striking six fours and two sixes. She hammered four boundaries in the opening over and later sealed the victory with a six off Shimako Kato.India had promoted Kamalini and Fulmali up the order, but the move did not pay off, with Kamalini dismissed for a duck and Fulmali scoring six. Shafali then combined with Richa Ghosh, who came in at No. 4, to complete the chase in a hurry.The pair shared a warm hug after the winning hit before crossing over to greet the Japanese players. Japan’s two wickets offered a small positive from an otherwise difficult outing.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India script history at Asian Games, register their biggest T20I win
articles.summary: Cricket News: India Women rewrote their T20I record books with a crushing eight-wicket victory over Japan, completing a 58-run chase in just five overs to register .
articles.body: India Women rewrote their T20I record books with a crushing eight-wicket victory over Japan, completing a 58-run chase in just five overs to register their biggest win by balls remaining. The defending champions finished the quarter-final with 90 balls to spare, surpassing their previous mark of 84 balls against Thailand in 2022.The record-breaking win at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Friday also sent India into the semi-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, where they will face Bangladesh on Sunday for a place in the medal match.India’s biggest T20I wins by balls remainingBalls remainingOpponentVenueYear90JapanNisshin202684ThailandSylhet202270BangladeshHangzhou202369Sri LankaSylhet202268PakistanDubai2026Shree Charani leads India’s bowling demolitionAfter winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers bundled Japan out for 57 in 19.5 overs. Shree Charani led the attack with four wickets, while Shafali Verma claimed two. Shreyanka Patil and Deepti Sharma picked up a wicket each.Ayaka Kato-Stafford top-scored for Japan with 25 off 47 deliveries, but the rest of the batting line-up struggled to cope with India’s disciplined bowling. Japan lost wickets at regular intervals and were unable to post a challenging total.Shafali seals record win in five oversIndia’s chase was swift and emphatic. Shafali Verma smashed an unbeaten 40 off just 15 balls, including four boundaries and two sixes, to put India firmly in control. India lost Gunalan Kamalini for a duck and Bharti Fulmali for six, but Japan could not capitalise on those breakthroughs. Richa Ghosh joined Shafali and scored an unbeaten 12 off six balls.With one run needed, Shafali finished the contest in style, launching Shimako Kato over long-on for a six. India reached 59/2 in five overs, sealing the win with 90 deliveries remaining.India’s record victory sets up a semi-final clash against Bangladesh, while Pakistan will take on Sri Lanka in the other last-four encounter on Sunday. The semi-final line-up mirrors the Women’s Asia Cup 2026, where the same four teams reached the last four.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Parthiv Patel frontrunner for chief selector if Ajit Agarkar, BCCI fail to agree extension
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong candidate to replace Ajit Agarkar as the men's senior selection committee chai.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong candidate to replace Ajit Agarkar as the men's senior selection committee chairman if the incumbent and the BCCI don't reach an extension agreement.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Parthiv's name has been circulating in Indian cricket's power corridors for the last six months when key figures were preparing for life after Agarkar. While an extension for the Mumbaikar wasn't off the table back then, a strong cosensus had been reached on Parthiv as the possible successor for the top job.If everything falls into place, Parthiv will be the most senior member of the panel with 25 Tests. SS Das played 23 Tests, RP Singh made 14 appearances while Pragyan Ojha and Ajay Ratra had 24 and 6 caps, respectively. The Indian cricket board has remained tight-lipped on the matter but clarity could be expected in the coming weeks.Agarkar picked the squads for the ODIs and T20Is against West Indies, and the Rest of India team for the Irani Cup and strong murmurs suggest this could well have been his last selection meeting. The former India cricketer attended the India-Afghanistan T20Is in Delhi, accompanied by selectors RP and Ratra. The second game of the series was also attended by ICC Chairman Jay Shah, BCCI President Mithun Manhas and Vice-President Rajeev Shukla.After the Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday, Shukla was brief on the topic, "AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors."Agarkar recently missed the high-profile review meeting attended by the Indian cricket board's top brass, head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, CoE head VVS Laxman. While the BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia downplayed the chief selector's absence saying he was out of town, those tracking developments believe it "doesn't add up"."You had everyone available there. It's not every day you get the key figures of Indian cricket under the same roof. Head coach travelled from Delhi, Laxman travelled, and Gill and Iyer both juggled their commitments. Mithun Manhas travelled too. So it was a bit strange that the chairman of the men's senior selection committee wasn't there when key issues were on the table. It just doesn't add up," said a source close to developments.Indian cricket is staring at a crucial 12 months in the build-up to the 2027 edition of the ODI World Cup and the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. While a section believes continuity with Agarkar is need of the hour, there are some influential voices keen to hand the reigns to Parthiv.The former India keeper is currently serving as assistant and batting coach at Gujarat Titans and commentating when his schedule permits. It is understood that Parthiv was likely to get a bigger role in the IPL franchise from the next cycle but if the selector role materialises, GT will probably have to explore different options.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: BCCI to take call on Ajit Agarkar's future after AGM authorisation, confirms Rajeev Shukla
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection comm.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee headed by Ajit Agarkar, vice-president Rajeev Shukla confirmed after the Board's 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday."Arun Singh Dhumal, Majumdar retain IPL governing council posts; AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors," Shukla said after attending the meeting at the BCCI headquarters.BCCI president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, Bengal Cricket Association president Sourav Ganguly, and Jharkhand State Cricket Association secretary Saurabh Tiwary were among the officials present at the AGM.Agarkar was appointed chairman of the men's senior selection committee in July 2023, and his contract is scheduled to end next month.If his tenure ends without an extension, the BCCI will not be able to appoint a new chairman immediately. The Board will first have to advertise the position and then conduct interviews before naming a replacement, making the appointment process likely to take some time.As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, former India wicketkeeper-batter Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong contender to replace Agarkar if the BCCI and the current chairman do not agree on an extension.If appointed, Parthiv would become the most experienced member of the current selection panel with 25 Test appearances. The other members are SS Das (23 Tests), RP Singh (14 Tests), Pragyan Ojha (24 Tests) and Ajay Ratra (6 Tests).The selectors announced India's squads for the upcoming home white-ball series against West Indies earlier this week. Their next major responsibility will be selecting India's Test and India 'A' squads for the tour of New Zealand in October and November.India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests against New Zealand, while India 'A' will play three unofficial Tests against New Zealand 'A' in a shadow tour ahead of the two-match Test series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Brewdog's unpaid workers to receive nothing after takeover deal
articles.summary: Administrators say about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and holiday pay and £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.
articles.body:
Former Brewdog staff and several creditors of the collapsed Scottish beer giant are not expected to receive anything from the administration process.

A report from administrators AlixPartners said there were "insufficient funds" for payouts to those owed money by Brewdog's retail arm.

The Aberdeenshire-based brewer had more than £500m of debts when it was sold in March to US drinks firm Tilray in a £33m rescue deal.

Administrators said about £489,000 was owed for staff wages and accrued holiday pay. A further £2.4m was owed to HMRC for unpaid VAT.

From a £1bn dream to a brutal collapse: How Brewdog hit the rocks

BrewDog's takeover saw 38 bars close across the UK and £20m in unpaid bills left to hundreds of UK businesses .

Unpaid businesses ranged from coffee shops, bakeries and laundry services, to lawyers, councils and holiday parks.

Creditors included West Ham United FC, Lord's Cricket Ground and Manchester University.

AlixPartners said there were now "insufficient funds" for preferential creditors to be repaid.

This is due to lower than expected funds raised through sales of Brewdog assets and increased costs during the administration period.

The administrators cited unforeseen costs around the security of closed Brewdog pubs after a number of "unauthorised occupiers" gained access.

AlixPartners said it worked with landlords and lawyers to remove them.

The report highlights small amounts of money raised through asset sales. These include:

A 7.8 acre field in Potterton, Aberdeenshire, which sold to a local farmer for £41,300

Nine Brewdog vehicles of "old age and varying roadworthiness" that made only £6,250 from just one sale. The rest were abandoned.

A settlement involving drinks equipment sold to Marylebone Cricket Club, which owns Lords, which generated £62,000.

Parent company BrewDog PLC is still expected to pay its preferential creditor, HMRC, in full for £3.66m tax owed - mainly VAT and excise duty.

Brewdog's biggest debt was to financial services group HSBC, which was owed more than £61m across various banking arms.

It has recovered tens of millions of pounds, but still faces an estimated shortfall of £16.8m.

The report noted that this could be reduced through asset sales in the United States.

Private equity backer TSG, which took a 22% stake in the brewer in 2017, is set to lose £27.6m.

Brewdog also owes around £190m to unsecured creditors. They are expected to receive less than a penny in the pound of what they are owed.

In March 440 staff were made redundant and 736 employees transferred to Tilray, after the US firm bought Brewdog's brand and UK operation.

Eleven bars were retained as part of the sale while 38 other pubs closed immediately.

Former staff can claim for unpaid wages through the UK government's Insolvency Service.

AlixPartners said workers had been given information on this support.

Brewdog's collapse also rendered the shares of about 200,000 crowdfunding investors worthless.

Earlier this year, Alixpartners confirmed that investors in the Equity for Punks scheme would get no return on their shares.

Investors typically spent about £500 on shares - although others invested much larger sums - in return for a stake in the company, discounts and perks.

The administrators stated these shares now had "no value".

Brewdog, which was founded in 2007 by friends James Watt and Martin Dickie, had four breweries and about 100 pubs across the world at its peak.

Watt said he was "heartbroken" after the collapse and apologised to staff and investors.

Brewdog's owner Tilray has been approached for comment.

articles.title: 'Subah Jalandhar, shaam nu Dilli': Abhishek Sharma's fiery Punjabi pep talk before 30-ball century goes viral - Watch
articles.summary: Cricket News: Abhishek Sharma lit up a dead rubber with a 30-ball century as India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Afghanistan with a 127-run win in the third and.
articles.body: Abhishek Sharma lit up a dead rubber with a 30-ball century as India completed a 3-0 series sweep over Afghanistan with a 127-run win in the third and final T20I in Delhi on Thursday.Abhishek tore into the Afghanistan bowling attack, scoring 108 off just 34 balls with 11 sixes. His innings took India to 221 for 7 after Afghanistan chose to field first.Afghanistan's batting struggled once again, just as it had in the first two matches, and the visitors were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs.After the match, BCCI posted a video of Abhishek giving a passionate pre-match speech during the team huddle.In the video shared by the BCCI, Abhishek can be seen addressing his teammates during the pre-match huddle in Punjabi and urged them to finish the series strongly."I'm going to speak Punjabi," Sharma declared to his assembled teammates. "So boys, today we are going to play like soormas. Soorma means warriors. The way we've been playing this entire series, that's exactly how we need to finish it today.""Warriors never show mercy to anyone. We aren't letting them off the hook today. It's the last match of the series, look at the crowd, we are going to give them full entertainment. Alright? Otherwise, let's smash it. Chak de phatte, nap de killi, subah Jalandhar, shaam nu Dilli," he added.Abhishek's hundred was the fastest by an Indian in T20Is, breaking Rohit Sharma's 35-ball record set in 2017.It was also the fastest T20I century by a player from a Test-playing nation against another Test-playing nation, going past New Zealand's Finn Allen, who had reached the milestone in 33 balls against South Africa earlier this year.With India having already wrapped up the series, Abhishek's innings added excitement to the final game and capped off a dominant performance before the team heads to the Asian Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: County Championship: Somerset title hopes dented with defeat at Yorkshire
articles.summary: Somerset's hopes of a first-ever County Championship title are dented with a heavy defeat at Yorkshire.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division One, Headingley (day four)

Yorkshire 212 & 275: Hill 89, Bess 77; Overton 3-44

Somerset 201: Cliff 8-76 & 101: Lammonby 32; Coad 4-33

Yorkshire (19 pts) beat Somerset (3 pts) by 185 runs

A relentless Yorkshire bowling performance put a significant dent in Somerset's County Championship title challenge, the hosts consigning the pre-game Division One leaders to a hammer-blow defeat at Headingley.

Somerset, who were chasing 287, started day four on 73-3, quickly slipped to 79-6 and were later bowled out for 101 just before 12:00 BST to lose by 185 runs.

A third defeat of the season, and a second against Yorkshire, means that Warwickshire now lead Division One by 11 points from second-placed Somerset, who have never won this title. Nottinghamshire will also be in the mix come next week's final round, even if they lose against Sussex later on Friday.

For the mid-table White Rose, they claimed their fifth win in 13 games and backed up May's success at Taunton. New ball seamers Ben Coad and Ben Cliff starred on Friday, Coad finishing with four wickets and Cliff three.

Outstanding Cliff ended with career-best match figures of 11-105, the 13th best match analysis in his county's first-class history.

Cliff and Coad struck in the space of five balls inside the day's opening half hour, putting Yorkshire on course for a 19-point haul to Somerset's three.

They removed not out batters Tom Lammonby and Tom Abell as Somerset lost two wickets for the addition of only three runs - 76-5.

Lammonby was squared up and caught behind off Cliff for 32 before Abell looped a catch up to backward point off the shoulder of the bat against Coad.

And when Coad struck again almost three overs later, at the end of the 39th, Somerset were in significant trouble, with James Rew caught at second slip on the drive.

Yorkshire came into day four knowing they had the edge but one wicket they were desperate for was that of Craig Overton, who had broken their hearts back in July here with a stunning 79 not out off 30 balls in the Vitality Blast quarter-final.

Cliff got him caught behind pushing forwards in the 42nd over for five, also trapping Lewis Gregory lbw three balls later.

At 88-8, it was all but game over under an overcast Headingley sky but not quite matching the gloomy Somerset outlook.

The Overton and Gregory wickets were Cliff's 10th and 11th in the match following his eight in the first innings.

Like Overton, Migael Pretorius had scored a first-innings fifty. But George Hill had him caught behind, leaving Somerset at 92-9.

Matthew Revis then wrapped things up by yorking Jake Ball, with day four lasting only 82 minutes in all.

Somerset face Surrey at the Cooper Associates County Ground, Taunton, in the final round of fixtures, which starts on Thursday, while Yorkshire can continue to play the role of spoilers when they travel to face Nottinghamshire at Trent Bridge.

ECB Reporters' Network supported by Rothesay.

articles.title: 100 years of BCCI! Indian cricket board to form committee for grand year-long celebrations
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) will complete 100 years in 2028 and plans to form a committee to organise year-long celebrations. The.
articles.body: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) will complete 100 years in 2028 and plans to form a committee to organise year-long celebrations. The topic was brought up for discussion during the final phase of the Annual General Meeting (AGM) by an influential administrator and the office bearers unanimously agreed on grand celebrations, commencing in December 2027."The General Body has initiated the process for the BCCI centenary celebrations in 2028. The centenary will be celebrated through a year-long programme, commencing in December 2027 continuing through 2028, marking a landmark milestone in the history of Indian Cricket." read the media advisory.The administrator argued that the BCCI should think globally about the celebrations because of the role it has played in the growth of cricket in different regions."We are talking about the BCCI. 100 years is no ordinary feat. It deserves the grandest celebration which needs careful consideration. Not a one-off affair. We should think about taking it global and plan as early as December 2027," the administrator told the gathering at the BCCI Headquarters on Friday.In addition to the centenary celebrations, the BCCI decided that the 2027 edition of the Indian Premier League — the cash-rich league's 20th — will also be celebrated grandly."The General Body unanimously took a call to celebrate the upcoming 20th edition of IPL in 2027 in a grand way," read another statement in the ten-point advisory.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: After getting just one international in 2026-27 season, MCA asks BCCI to allot more matches to Wankhede Stadium
articles.summary: Cricket News: MUMBAI: The Mumbai Cricket Association has requested the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to allot more international matches to the Wankh.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Mumbai Cricket Association has requested the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to allot more international matches to the Wankhede Stadium in future schedules, while also seeking to be informed before matches are awarded to other venues in Mumbai.The request was made during the 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the BCCI at its headquarters on the Wankhede Stadium premises. MCA secretary Unmesh Khanvilkar submitted a letter, a copy of which is with TOI, putting forward the association's demands.The MCA's request comes after Wankhede was allotted only one international match in India's 2026-27 home season. The stadium will host the third and final ODI between India and Zimbabwe on January 9 next year.The MCA, which celebrated the Wankhede Stadium's 50th anniversary in January 2025, has pointed out that the venue is a permanent Test Centre and has asked the BCCI to consider giving it more international matches.“The MCA sincerely thanks the BCCI for the international matches allotted to Mumbai over the years and for its continued confidence in the Association's hosting capabilities. As the Wankhede Stadium is a permanent Test Centre with a proud history of successfully staging marquee international fixtures, MCA would be grateful if the BCCI could consider allotting a greater number of international matches to the venue in future programmes. We remain committed to providing the highest standards of facilities and match operations for players, officials, and spectators alike,” Khanvilkar has written.The MCA has also asked the BCCI to inform the association before awarding matches to stadiums and venues located within its jurisdiction, which includes Mumbai.The request comes after the BCCI announced a couple of days ago that the 2027 Women's Premier League will be held at the Brabourne Stadium, which is operated by the Cricket Club of India, from January 14 to February 27. Brabourne Stadium is located around 750 metres from Wankhede.The International Cricket Council has also recently awarded the inaugural Women's T20 Champions Trophy matches to Brabourne Stadium. The tournament is scheduled to be held from February 14 to 28.The MCA said being informed in advance would help it deal with queries from its members and other stakeholders and coordinate with the organisations involved in staging matches in Mumbai.“The MCA would be grateful if, as a matter of courtesy, the Association could be kept informed whenever matches are scheduled at stadiums or venues located within its jurisdiction. Such communication would assist MCA in addressing queries from its members and stakeholders and would help foster smooth coordination and cooperation among all concerned,” the MCA has stated in its letter.MCA seeks Under-17 girls' tournamentThe MCA has also asked the BCCI to introduce an Under-17 girls' tournament in its domestic cricket calendar.The BCCI currently conducts a Girls Under-15 tournament, with the next age-group competitions starting at the Under-19 level.“The MCA requests the BCCI to consider introducing a structured Under-17 Girls Cricket Tournament at the national level. Such a tournament would provide an important competitive platform for young female cricketers, strengthen the talent development pathway, and further support the growth of women's cricket across the country,” Khanvilkar has stated in his letter.“We request the Board to give due consideration to the above matters and look forward to a positive response,” Khanvilkar concluded in his letter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
